summary: Spain's investor visa/residence scheme (Ley 14/2013, Sep 2013 - 3 Apr 2025) and the Investor Visa for Italy (art. 26-bis immigration act, from 2017). Spain: laws and amendments are complete; numbers come from one 2015 ministry report, seven government answers to Parliament (consular visas by year, route, region and some nationalities) and April 2024 press releases whose much larger counts (14,576 real-estate 'golden visas' 2013-2023) are undefined and do not match the consular series (6,272 real-estate visas 2013-2023). Italy: every legal change is documented from Normattiva; official uptake data are tiny and stale (13 applications to end-2019, 9 start-up-route applications to end-2021).

events.title: Spain creates investor visa and residence permit (Ley 14/2013)
events.description: Ley 14/2013 de apoyo a los emprendedores (BOE 28 Sep 2013), arts. 61-67, creates a visa and residence authorisation for non-EU investors: EUR 500,000 in property per applicant, EUR 2m public debt, EUR 1m shares or bank deposits, or a business project of general interest. In force the day after publication.
events.quote: Se entenderá como inversión significativa de capital aquella que cumpla con alguno de los siguientes supuestos

events.title: Ley 25/2015 widens Spain's investor visa: funds route, right to work, five-year renewals
events.description: Rewrites arts. 63-67 Ley 14/2013: adds EUR 1m in Spanish investment or venture-capital funds; shares must be in companies with real business activity; one-year visa allowing residence and work; investor's representative for business projects; pre-contract property route with 6-month visa; residence authorisations granted by the DG for Migration and processed by UGE-CE; renewals for successive five-year periods. In force 30 Jul 2015.
events.quote: podrán solicitar la renovación de la autorización de residencia por periodos sucesivos de cinco años

events.title: Government confirms former Mexican president Peña Nieto holds a Spanish investor residence permit
events.description: Answer to a parliamentary question: Enrique Peña Nieto holds an investor residence authorisation under Ley 14/2013, based on a EUR 570,000 commercial property in Madrid; the government knows of no other assets.
events.quote: el interesado acreditó la inversión por valor de 570.000 euros, libre de cargas y gravámenes, en un local comercial ubicado en Madrid

events.title: Spain says it is not issuing investor visas to Russian nationals
events.description: After Russia's invasion of Ukraine, the government tells Parliament that no Ley 14/2013 investor (capital, real-estate, business project) or entrepreneur visas are currently being issued to Russian nationals. Date is the date of the answer; when issuing stopped is not stated.
events.quote: En la actualidad no se están expidiendo visados amparados en la Ley 14/2013

events.title: Initial investor residence authorisation extended from two to three years
events.description: Ley 28/2022 (start-ups law) amends art. 67.1 Ley 14/2013 so the first investor residence authorisation lasts three years. In force the day after publication (BOE 22 Dec 2022).
events.quote: La autorización inicial de residencia para inversores tendrá una duración de tres años

events.title: Council of Ministers studies report to abolish real-estate golden visas
events.description: The Housing Minister presents a report to the Council of Ministers proposing to amend Ley 14/2013 to end residence permits for property investment, citing housing pressure (up to 7.1% of home sales in Marbella and 5.3% in Barcelona linked to such investments) and 14,576 grants since 2013.
events.location: item 'Fin de las golden visa inmobiliarias'
events.quote: El Consejo de ministros ha sido informado sobre la propuesta de modificación del régimen de residencia por inversión (Golden Visa)

events.title: Italy creates investor visa (art. 26-bis immigration act)
events.description: The 2017 Budget Law (L. 232/2016, art. 1, c. 148) inserts art. 26-bis into the immigration act: entry outside quotas and a two-year permit for non-EU investors putting EUR 2m into government bonds, EUR 1m into an Italian company (EUR 500k for an innovative start-up) or donating EUR 1m. Text in force 1 Jan 2017; applications only possible once the procedure was set up (see later events).
events.quote: sono consentiti, al di fuori delle quote di cui all'articolo 3, comma 4, agli stranieri che intendono effettuare

events.title: Implementing decree sets up the investor visa procedure and Committee
events.description: Inter-ministerial decree (Economic Development, Interior, Foreign Affairs) of 21 Jul 2017 defines eligible investments and creates the Investor Visa Committee that issues the nulla osta.
events.quote: Questo è stato emanato dal Ministro dello Sviluppo Economico

events.title: Investor Visa for Italy portal opens for applications
events.description: After the Committee's first meeting and approval of the manual on 16 Nov 2017, the online platform investorvisa.mise.gov.it launches on 14 Dec 2017, marking the operational start of the programme.

events.title: Italy halves investor visa thresholds for companies and start-ups
events.description: D.L. 34/2020 ('Decreto Rilancio'), art. 38(10), cuts the company route from EUR 1m to EUR 500k and the innovative start-up route from EUR 500k to EUR 250k. In force 19 May 2020; converted by L. 77/2020.
events.quote: sono sostituite dalle seguenti: "di almeno euro 500.000 in strumenti rappresentativi del capitale di una società costituita e operante in Italia mantenuto per almeno due anni ovvero di almeno euro 250.000"

events.title: Investor visa opened to representatives of legal persons; holders get self-employment rights
events.description: Art. 40-quater D.L. 76/2020 (added by conversion law L. 120/2020): investment may be made on behalf of a legal person the applicant represents (subject to reciprocity check); permit holders get the rights of the self-employment permit and a five-year exemption from the integration agreement and continuous-stay requirements.
events.quote: in nome proprio o per conto della persona giuridica che legalmente rappresentano

events.title: Investor Visa for Italy suspended for Russian and Belarusian citizens
events.description: Order of the Committee chair of 14 Jul 2023, citing European Commission Recommendation C(2022) 2028, suspends the programme for Russian and Belarusian citizens.
events.quote: Notice is hereby given of the suspension of the program for Russian and Belarusian citizens as per the order of the Chairman of the Committee dated 07/14/2023

events.title: Suspension extended to dual nationals holding a Russian or Belarusian passport
events.description: Following a Foreign Ministry (MAECI) note of 20 Mar 2024 implementing EU Recommendation C(2022) 2028, the programme is suspended for non-EU citizens with a second, Russian or Belarusian, passport.
events.quote: Following the MAECI note of 20/03/2024 implementing the EU Recommendation C (2022) 2028

events.title: Italian venture-capital funds added to the EUR 500k investor visa route
events.description: L. 193/2024 (annual competition law 2023), art. 35, rewrites art. 26-bis(1)(b) so the EUR 500,000 route covers Italian venture-capital funds as well as companies; start-up threshold stays EUR 250,000. In force 18 Dec 2024.
events.quote: di una società o di un fondo di venture capital costituiti e operanti in Italia

programs.name: Spain investor visa and residence authorisation (visado y autorización de residencia para inversores, Ley 14/2013, 'golden visa')
programs.notes: Residence (not citizenship) for non-EU investors under arts. 61-67 of Ley 14/2013 (in force 29 Sep 2013). Routes: EUR 500,000 real estate per applicant; EUR 2m Spanish public debt; EUR 1m in shares of Spanish companies or in Spanish bank deposits; from 30 Jul 2015 also EUR 1m in Spanish investment/venture-capital funds; business project of general interest (no fixed amount). Visas issued by consulates (Foreign Ministry); residence authorisations granted in Spain by the Directorate-General for Migration and processed by the Unidad de Grandes Empresas y Colectivos Estratégicos (UGE-CE). Visa 1 year; initial authorisation 2 years (3 years from 23 Dec 2022); renewals 2 years, then 5 years from 30 Jul 2015. Family members got derivative permits. The law gave no shortcut to citizenship. Arts. 63-67 emptied by Ley Orgánica 1/2025 (in force 3 Apr 2025); existing permits may be renewed. Official statistics are scattered: one 2015 ministry report, parliamentary answers, and 2024 press releases whose counts do not match each other (consular visas vs all authorisations).

programs.name: Investor Visa for Italy (visto per investitori, art. 26-bis D.Lgs. 286/1998)
programs.notes: Entry visa and two-year 'per investitori' residence permit, renewable for three years at a time, for non-EU nationals who invest EUR 2m in Italian government bonds, EUR 500k (EUR 1m until 18 May 2020) in an Italian company (from 18 Dec 2024 also an Italian venture-capital fund), EUR 250k (EUR 500k until 18 May 2020) in an innovative start-up, or donate EUR 1m to a public-interest project; investment must be made within 3 months of arrival and held for 2 years. Legal basis in force 1 Jan 2017 (L. 232/2016, art. 1, c. 148); implementing decree 21 Jul 2017; applications run through an online portal from 14 Dec 2017, vetted by an inter-ministerial Committee chaired by the ministry of enterprise (MISE, now MIMIT), which issues a nulla osta. No real-estate route. Applications free of charge. Holders may apply for an EU long-term permit after 5 years of holding the investment (portal); no special route to citizenship. Suspended for Russian and Belarusian citizens from 14 Jul 2023 and for dual nationals with a Russian or Belarusian passport from 20 Mar 2024. Very low uptake: 13 applications to end-2019 (latest official total found).

new_indicators.name: Investor visas issued
new_indicators.definition: Entry or long-stay visas issued by consulates to main investors under an investor-residence programme in a period. Excludes residence permits granted in-country, renewals and family members unless noted.
new_indicators.notes: Needed for Spain, where consular visas (Foreign Ministry) and residence authorisations granted in Spain (Ministry of Inclusion) are counted separately and the two series differ widely.

gaps: Spain: no official annual series of residence authorisations for investors granted in Spain (Ministry of Inclusion / UGE-CE) after 2018. Law 14/2013 required an annual report but only the April 2015 one was published (also noted by the European Commission, SWD(2019) 5).

Spain: the April 2024 government figures (14,576 real-estate golden visas 2013-2023; 2,017 in 2022; 3,273 in 2023) are not defined; whether they include renewals and/or family members could not be established. The consular visa series given to Parliament is 3-4 times lower for the same years.
Spain: no official nationality breakdown after Feb 2018 except TI-España's FOI-based summary (to Sep 2023) and an unquantified list of nationalities for 2024.
Spain: no figures for the last months before abolition (Oct 2024 - 2 Apr 2025), nor for renewals of existing permits after 3 April 2025.

Spain: the Ministry of Inclusion Tableau dashboards on Ley 14/2013 permits ('stock_ley14', 'flujo_ley14'), to which the government pointed in its answer to question 184/15650 (Nov 2024), could not be read: inclusion.gob.es blocks scripted access and the Tableau Public views return 'missing view'.
Spain: no government fee data collected (visa and authorisation fees).

Italy: no official totals of applications, nulla osta, visas or permits after December 2019; MIMIT's annual start-up reports stopped covering the investor visa after the 2022 edition, and the programme portal publishes no statistics.
Italy: no data on donations made, money invested by route, or permits renewed/revoked; no Interior Ministry permit statistics for the 'per investitori' permit type were found.

Italy: the WebSearch budget for this session ran out partway through, so Italian parliamentary questions (Camera/Senato) and Italian press reports on investor visa numbers were not searched systematically.
leads: Spain Ministry of Inclusion infographics (Tableau): https://www.inclusion.gob.es/documents/3976286/3994787/infografias.html?stock_ley14 and ?flujo_ley14 (stock and flow of Ley 14/2013 authorisations; open in a normal browser).

Congreso answer 184/6124 (May 2020) with an annex of Ley 14/2013 visas by country, consulate and visa code (REM, RFI, RIN, RIV...): https://www.congreso.es/l14p/e2/e_0026374_n_000.pdf - needs the code legend to interpret.
Congreso 186/000305 (XV Legislatura): request for the Housing Ministry report on golden visas and housing (April 2024); the report itself was not found online.

European Commission SWD(2019) 5 (staff working document on investor schemes; describes Spain and Italy): https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52019SC0005 (Wayback copy downloads).
Senado de España written questions on golden visas (not searched).
Italy: Decreto direttoriale 14 novembre 2017 naming the Committee members: https://www.mimit.gov.it/images/stories/normativa/Decreto-direttoriale-INVESTOR-VISA.pdf

Italy: Camera dei deputati / Senato interrogazioni on 'visto per investitori' numbers (search aic.camera.it and senato.it); a freedom-of-information (FOIA) request to MIMIT's Investor Visa Committee secretariat would likely be needed for post-2019 figures.
